title: IR-Runbook-Scheduled-Task-Persistence
summary: Original short-response guidance for suspicious Windows scheduled tasks used for persistence.
content:
## 1.1 [Immediate] Preserve and contain the task
Record the task name, author, trigger, action, and creation time before disabling a task. Isolate the endpoint if its action launches confirmed malicious code.

## 2.1 [Investigate] Validate task origin and execution
Inspect task XML, referenced binaries or scripts, creator account, and task-scheduler operational logs. Compare the action and trigger with the approved endpoint baseline.

## 3.1 [Recover] Remove unauthorized persistence
Disable and remove confirmed malicious tasks after evidence collection, quarantine their payloads, and rotate credentials used to create or run them.
